subquestions.text_open: 9.1 The benzoin condensation is familiar. Give the SMILES of the four key intermediates in the catalytic cycle shown.

text_images.description: Under NEt_3, 'CC[N+]1=CSC(CCO)=C1' gives 'CC[N+]1=[C-]SC(CCO)=C1'. Reaction with '[H]C(C1=CC=CC=C1CCC(C)=O)=O' gives A; proton transfer gives B; B gives C; proton transfer gives D; D gives 'O=C1C(O)(C)CCC2=CC=CC=C21' and regenerates 'CC[N+]1=[C-]SC(CCO)=C1'. SMILES/structure strings shown: 'CC[N+]1=[C-]SC(CCO)=C1'.

subquestions.text_open: 9.3 Formaldehyde reacts poorly directly with NHCs. The reaction shown introduces a fragment equivalent to formaldehyde. Give the SMILES of the three key intermediates between the five-carbon aldose substrate and intermediate X.

text_images.description: 'O[C@H]1[C@@H](O)[C@H](O)C(O)OC1' and 'O=C(C1=CC=CC=C1)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2' give 'C[N+]1=CSC(C)=C1C.[I-]' under 20 mol% 'O=C(C1=CC=CC=C1)CC(C([H])=O)C2=CC=CC=C2', 20 mol% K_2CO_3, MeCN, 130 °C, μW, 10 min. Intermediate X: 'O/C([H])=C1N(C)C(C)=C(C)S\1'.

subquestions.text_open: 9.4 When the reactant is not an aldehyde, NHCs can catalyze other reactions. The following reaction of an α-hydroxy ketone is NHC-catalyzed; the catalytic cycle is shown, and G carries one positive charge. 9.4.1 Compare the molecular formulas of reactants and products and identify the small-molecule product Y.

text_images.description: Reaction of 'O=C(C(C)(C)O)/C=C/C1=C(C)C=C(C)C=C1C' and 'CC1NCCCC1' under 10 mol% of the listed NHC catalyst, 10 mol% of the listed hydroxamic reagent, and 20 mol% DBU, DCM, room temperature gives 'C[C@@H]1N(C(CCC2=C(C)C=C(C)C=C2C)=O)CCCC1' and 'C[C@H]1NCCCC1'. SMILES/structure strings shown: 'CC1=CC(C)=CC(C)=C1[N+]2=CN3C(CCC3)=N2.[O-]Cl(=O)(=O)=O', 'O=C(CO1)N(O)[C@@H]([C@@H]1C2)C3=C2C=CC=C3'.

Catalytic cycle: 'C[C@@H]1NCCCC1' reacts with H to give 'O=C(N1[C@@H](C)CCCC1)CCC2=C(C)C=C(C)C=C2C' and the cyclic hydroxamic product. The azolium catalyst and DBU form the NHC. The cyclic hydroxamic product and G give H and regenerate the NHC after loss of [H^+]. The NHC reacts with the α-hydroxy ketone to give E; E gives Y and F; protonation of F gives G. SMILES/structure strings shown: 'O=C1N(O)[C@H](C(C=CC=C2)=C2C3)[C@H]3OC1', 'O=C1N(O)[C@H](C(C=CC=C2)=C2C3)[C@H]3OC1', 'CC1=CC(C)=CC(C)=C1[N+]2=CN3C(CCC3)=N2', 'CC1=CC(C)=CC(C)=C1[N+]2=[C-]N3C(CCC3)=N2', 'CC1=CC(C)=CC(C)=C1[N+]2=[C-]N3C(CCC3)=N2', 'CC1=CC(C)=CC(C)=C1[N+]2=[C-]N3C(CCC3)=N2', 'O=C(C(C)(C)O)/C=C/C1=C(C)C=C(C)C=C1C'.

subquestions.text_open: 9.4.2 Give the SMILES of the four key intermediates E, F, G, and H.

9.5 With a vicinal diketone substrate, the reaction mode changes again. Give the SMILES of the four key intermediates. NEt_3 acts only as a base with the thiazolium ion; the resulting NHC first reacts with the vicinal diketone. Two addition-elimination events occur and each is treated as one step; their tetrahedral intermediates need not be shown. The NHC formed in the initial acid-base step also need not be shown.

text_images.description: '[Ar]C(C=C)=O' and 'O=C(C(C1=CC=CC=C1)=O)C2=CC=CC=C2' react under 'C[N+]1=CSC2=C1CCCCC2' and NEt_3 to give '[Ar]C(C(C(C1=CC=CC=C1)=O)CC(C2=CC=CC=C2)=O)=O'.
